item.title: We Are All Going To Die: End-of-Life Option Act — Thu Oct 29, 1:00 PM — Petaluma Library
item.description:
Join us for Part 3 of our three-part Death and Dying series. Learn about the End-of-Life Option Act with Dennis Pocekay M.D. and co-hosted by the Village Network of Petaluma The California End of Life Option Act allows a terminally ill California resident to request a drug from a physician that will end the patient's life. People who follow the steps of the law will not be considered to have committed suicide, and physicians who prescribe the aid-in-dying drug will not be subject to legal liability or professional sanction. This presentation will review the eligibility, procedure, and documentation requirements of the law.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Sip & Seed Volunteer Night at Clif Family Winery — Thu Oct 29, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Sip & Seed Volunteer Night at Clif Family Winery Tasting Room invites guests to explore seed saving with the Napa County Seed Library. This free event introduces three seed varieties, including Jalapeño Grande peppers and Huerfano Bliss melon grown on the farm. Guests can learn about seed preservation from Lauren of the Napa County Seed Library and Clif Family grower Tessa Henry, then participate in hands-on seed cleaning, sorting and processing. The evening also offers opportunities to ask questions, connect with fellow gardeners and enjoy wine by the glass and food from the Bruschetteria food truck, available for purchase. The event runs from 4 to 7 p.m., with an RSVP requested.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Petaluma's Houdini Séance: The Centennial Gathering — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
item.description:
Some traditions are too good to stay buried.
For decades, Petaluma had its own connection to the afterlife.
Friday, October 30 7 pm – 9 pm
Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)
Get Tickets
Beginning in 1964, legendary local journalist Bill Soberanes—affectionately known as “Mr. Petaluma”—gathered believers, skeptics, magicians, and the simply curious each Halloween season for an annual séance attempting to contact the spirit of Harry Houdini. Many of these spirited gatherings took place right here at the Petaluma Museum.
But Petaluma’s fascination with the mysterious and fantastic goes back even further. Spiritualists were holding séances here in the 19th century, and local legend even has it that Houdini himself once performed in town.
Now, 100 years after Houdini’s death, we’re bringing the tradition back to life.
Join us on October 30—the eve of the centennial of Houdini’s death—for an unforgettable evening of history, m

If you bring your own fabric, please make sure it is a stable woven. We recommend flannels \(like an old flannel shirt, pajama bottoms, or a pillow case\) for cozier experience when using the heating pads, but quilting cottons and linens would work as well. We have 5 sewing machines available for the workshop. If you have your own machine you would like to bring, please let us so know so we can set up the room accordingly. item.title: Timely Wisdom — Sun Nov 8, 3:00 PM — The Glaser Center
item.description:
The Power of Storytelling in Troubling Times
We will explore storytelling as a creative way to wield the liberating power of the Dharma in our daily lives, especially in these troubling times.
Drawing on the lifelong commitments of Paula Arai’s research-based writing as a contemplative practice and Kathie Fischer’s focus on Zen practice in domestic and monastic modes, we will invite people to help us create our own community story about wielding the compassionate teaching of the Dharma in these times.
